entries.title: Ettore Tolomei, Prontuario dei nomi locali dell'Alto Adige, in Archivio per l'Alto Adige, annata XI (1916)
text: Ettore Tolomei's list of Italian names for the places of South Tyrol, as first printed in his own journal in 1916 and found online in full. Its introduction says the State must show that the new provinces are Italian “con la nomenclatura dei luoghi, con tutto ciò ch'è scritto, stampato, pubblico ed apparente in pubblico”.
The list ranks places by typeface: bold for the 204 communes, italics for mountains, valleys and waters. “Bozen – Bolzano” stands in bold.
facts: The 1916 volume of Tolomei's Archivio per l'Alto Adige; its 'Sommario dell'annata XI' lists 'Prontuario dei nomi locali dell'Alto Adige … Pag. 3', followed by Toniolo at p. 141 (notes 16, §1, [V])
Introduction: the State must make the new provinces' belonging evident 'con la nomenclatura dei luoghi, con tutto ciò ch'è scritto, stampato, pubblico ed apparente in pubblico' (notes 16, §1, [V])
The list ranks names by typeface: 'Il nero-distinto è dei principali di essi luoghi ossia dei 204 Comuni … Il corsivo è dei monti, valli, località, acque' (p. 35) (notes 16, §1, [V])
Tolomei counts '10.000 vocaboli' (p. 7); a snippet of E. Mori's PDF gives 16,735 toponyms [SS]: unsettled (notes 16, §1)
Notes 03 §4 believed the Prontuario was online only as a private PDF; this scan contradicts that (notes 16, §1)

Seen in the image (title spread): 'ARCHIVIO PER L'ALTO ADIGE CON AMPEZZO E LIVINALLONGO – Direttore Ettore Tolomei – Annata XI – 1916', a round stamp 'Biblioteca della Città di Trento'; on the left the Sommario; a large grey 'BPI' watermark across both pages.

Seen in the image (pp. 46–47): two columns per page of German names with Italian equivalents and grid references; 'Bozen – Bolzano (Bo a1)', 'Brixen – Bressanone (Kd1)' and 'Bruneck – Brunico (Br b3)' set in bold.
Seen in the image (pp. 34–35): a grid diagram of map sheet K with Klausen and Kastelruth; on p. 35 the three typefaces described, with 'Bozen – Bolzano; Aldein – Valdagno' in bold.

entries.title: La Domenica del Corriere, 23–30 October 1921, front cover: Il sacro rito del Brennero
text: The cover of the Domenica del Corriere for 23–30 October 1921, drawn by A. Beltrame: the king and his officers raise their hands before a boundary stone hung with flags. The caption has him swear “che questo Passo sarà eternamente nostro”.
A year before the March on Rome the Brenner was already staged as a sacred border, by the monarchy and the national press. The ceremony behind the drawing has not been identified.
facts: Cover of the Corriere della Sera's illustrated weekly, anno XXIII n. 43, caption: 'Il sacro rito del Brennero. Il Re giura sul confine della Patria: Giuriamo qui, tutti, per i nostri morti, per i nostri discendenti, che questo Passo sarà eternamente nostro', 'Disegno di A. Beltrame' (notes 16, §2, [V])
The event behind the drawing (date, place on the pass) is not established (notes 16, §4, Gaps)
Before fascism in power, the Brenner was already staged as a sacred border by monarchy and national press (notes 16, §4, [INF])

entries.title: Regio decreto 29 marzo 1923, n. 800: lezione ufficiale dei nomi dei comuni e di altre località dei territori annessi
text: The royal decree of 29 March 1923 that made the lists of Italian place names law in the annexed territories, signed by the king and Mussolini. State signs, stamps and seals use the Italian name. Where a second name is allowed it “deve tenere il secondo posto, fra parentesi, e non può essere scritto con caratteri più appariscenti di quelli del nome italiano”.
In the list, Chiusa has “Klausen” beside it and Sarentino “Sarnthein”. Number 555 reads only “Bolzano.”
facts: GU n. 99, 27 April 1923, whole issue; the decree makes the lists of official names law for the annexed territories (manifest; notes 16, §1, [V])
Art. 1: names not in the lists follow 'le forme adottate nei Prontuari e Repertori della Reale Società geografica italiana' (notes 16, §1, [V])
Art. 2: State 'insegne', 'timbri' and 'suggelli' use the names of the first column (notes 16, §1, [V])
Art. 3: the second name 'deve tenere il secondo posto, fra parentesi, e non può essere scritto con caratteri più appariscenti di quelli del nome italiano' (notes 16, §1, [V])

Seen in the image (p. 3334): two columns; left, 'Abbiamo decretato e decretiamo', arts. 1–4, 'Dato a Roma, addì 29 marzo 1923. Vittorio Emanuele. Mussolini'; right, 'Allegato n. 1 – Venezia Giulia – I. Nomi dei Comuni – Provincia di Trieste', some names with a second name beside them.

Seen in the image (p. 3353): 'Circondario di Bolzano – Mandamento di Bolzano: 555 — Bolzano.' with no second name beside it, while 'Sarentino Sarnthein', 'Chiusa Klausen' and 'Tiso Theis' have one; '568 — Vanga.'

entries.title: Bozner Nachrichten, 16 July 1923, page 1
text: The front page of the Bozner Nachrichten for 16 July 1923. In its right-hand column: “Gestern vorm. hielt Senator Tolomei im Stadttheater in Bozen eine Rede über die Entnationalisierung Südtirols”. The paper summarises the speech from the text given out by the Brennero agency.
This fixes where and when the measures for Alto Adige were read out: the city theatre of Bolzano, on the morning of Sunday 15 July 1923.
facts: Column 'Tolomei spricht über die Entnationalisierung Südtirols': 'Gestern vorm. hielt Senator Tolomei im Stadttheater in Bozen eine Rede über die Entnationalisierung Südtirols' (notes 16, §1, [V])
The paper summarises the speech 'aus dem von der Agentur Brennero ausgegebenen Wortlaut' (notes 16, §1, [V])
This is where and when the 'Provvedimenti per l'Alto Adige' were read out: the Stadttheater, Sunday morning 15 July 1923 (notes 16, §1)

entries.title: Regio decreto 1 ottobre 1923, n. 2185: Ordinamento dei gradi scolastici e dei programmi didattici dell'istruzione elementare
text: The school decree of 1 October 1923, signed “Mussolini — Gentile”. Article 17: “A cominciare dall'anno scolastico 1923-24, in tutte le prime classi delle scuole elementari alloglotte l'insegnamento sarà impartito in lingua italiana”, and one class more each year. The other language is left to added hours.
Article 25 wants Italian taught “di preferenza a maestri non alloglotti”. The decree's word for these schools and teachers is “alloglotti”: of another tongue.
facts: GU n. 250, 24 October 1923, whole issue (manifest)

Art. 17: 'A cominciare dall'anno scolastico 1923-24, in tutte le prime classi delle scuole elementari alloglotte l'insegnamento sarà impartito in lingua italiana', then one class more each year; the second language only 'in ore aggiunte' (notes 16, §3, [V])

entries.title: Der Landsmann, 27 October 1923, page 1
text: Three days after the school decree was published, the German daily of Bolzano leads with “Die Italianisierung unserer Volksschulen”. A boxed appeal, “Landsleute!”, is signed by the four German deputies, Reut-Nicolussi among them: “400 deutsche Schulen sind dem Untergange geweiht”.
The masthead reads “Der Landsmann”. The paper had been “Der Tiroler” until August 1923, when the name Tirol was banned.
facts: Headline 'Die Italianisierung unserer Volksschulen': the GU of 24 October publishes decree no. 2185, whose art. 17 imposes Italian in the first classes (notes 16, §3, [V])

Appeal 'Landsleute!', 'Bozen, am 26. Oktober 1923', signed by the deputies Dr. Reut-Nicolussi, Dr. von Walther, Graf Toggenburg, Dr. Karl Tinzl; '400 deutsche Schulen sind dem Untergange geweiht' (notes 16, §3, [V])
Commons files it as 'TIR' (Der Tiroler); the masthead reads 'Der Landsmann'. The paper had been renamed in August 1923 after the ban on the name 'Tirol' [W] (notes 16, §1)

Seen in the image: blackletter masthead 'Der Landsmann – Tagblatt der Deutschen südlich des Brenners', 'Nr. 246 – 24. Jahrg. – Bozen-Meran – Sonntag-Ausgabe – 27. Oktober 1923'; the headline across the page; the boxed appeal 'Landsleute!' at left; 'Der schwerste Schlag' and 'Die Volksschulreform' below.

entries.title: Adolf Hitler, Die Südtiroler Frage und das Deutsche Bündnisproblem
text: The title page of Hitler's pamphlet of 1926, “Die Südtiroler Frage und das Deutsche Bündnisproblem”, published by Eher in Munich and set in Fraktur. It put the alliance with Italy above South Tyrol.
Held for the other side of the question. The picture comes, by way of Wikimedia Commons, from page 97 of a later book that reprinted it.

entries.title: Il Podestà del Comune di S. Leonardo di Passiria, letter of 13 August 1926 on a clandestine German school
text: A letter from the podestà of San Leonardo in Passiria, 13 August 1926, subject “Scuole clandestine”. Ida Ladurner is to leave the commune by 16 August “per avere Ella aperto a S. Leonardo i.P. una scuola clandestina per l'insegnamento della lingua tedesca”.

The letterhead records another change of that year. The printed “IL SINDACO” is struck through and “IL PODESTA” set above it: the elected mayor replaced by an appointed one. The archive that holds the letter is not named.
facts: Archival letter, 'N. 8 ris.', subject 'Scuole clandestine', to Ida Ladurner: expulsion from the commune 'per avere Ella aperto a S. Leonardo i.P. una scuola clandestina per l'insegnamento della lingua tedesca', to take effect by 16 August (notes 16, §3, [V])
Commons calls it a 'Dismissal decree'; the text orders expulsion from the commune. The holding archive is not named (notes 16, §3)
The letterhead shows the 1926 change from elected mayor to appointed podestà: the printed office is struck out and the new one stamped above (notes 16, §3, [INF])

entries.title: Eduard Reut-Nicolussi, Tirol unterm Beil
text: The cover of Eduard Reut-Nicolussi's book against fascist rule in South Tyrol, dated 1928, in its people's edition. A red fasces rises over a black-and-red town, its axe-head uppermost: “Tirol unterm Beil”, Tyrol under the axe. The fascist emblem is turned against its maker, and the title is set in Fraktur.
Reut-Nicolussi was one of the four deputies who signed the school appeal of October 1923.
facts: Cover of Reut-Nicolussi's book against fascist rule in South Tyrol; dated 1928 on Commons; the copy is marked 'Volksausgabe' (notes 16, §6, [V])

entries.title: Bolzano – Scuole Elementari Regina Elena (the former Kaiserin-Elisabeth-Schule), postcard
text: A postcard of 1928 captioned “Bolzano - Scuole Elementari Regina Elena”. The building is the Kaiserin-Elisabeth-Schule, occupied by fascist squads on 1 October 1922 and renamed for the Italian queen. The building keeps its form; the new name is in the caption.
Today it is the Italian-language Scuola Dante Alighieri.
facts: The Kaiserin-Elisabeth-Schule on the Sparkassenstraße was occupied by fascist squads on 1 October 1922 and renamed 'Scuola Regina Elena'; today it is the Italian-language 'Scuola Dante Alighieri' [W] (notes 16, §3)

entries.title: Regia Scuola Tecnica Commerciale 'Duca di Pistoia', Bolzano: the building and its commodity-science laboratory
text: Three photographs from the archive of Italy's school-research institute: the Regia Scuola Tecnica Commerciale of Bolzano seen from Via San Quirino, and its commodity-science laboratory with pupils at flasks and microscopes. Over the door the lettering reads “R. SCUOLA TECNICA COMMERCIALE” and “DUCA DI PISTOIA”, between two coats of arms.
The building photograph is credited “Foto Waldmuller – Via Museo, 50 – Bolzano”. A search of the archive for Bolzano returned only these three.

entries.title: Mostra della Rivoluzione Fascista. Guida storica
text: The historical guide to the exhibition that marked ten years of the March on Rome, edited by Dino Alfieri and Luigi Freddi. Its cover sets a sculpted head of Mussolini on a black ground filled with “DU-CE” repeated on the diagonal. On page 31 Mussolini is quoted: “Tipica l'occupazione di Bolzano e la occupazione — squisitamente rivoluzionaria — di Trento”.
The scan held has only 33 pages, and its public-domain label is doubtful.
facts: Historical guide to the PNF exhibition for the tenth anniversary of the March on Rome, edited by Dino Alfieri and Luigi Freddi (notes 16, §4, [V])
p. 31, quoting Mussolini: 'Tipica l'occupazione di Bolzano e la occupazione — squisitamente rivoluzionaria — di Trento' (notes 16, §4, [V])

entries.title: Gravestone of Luigi (Alois) Gruber, former mayor of Vanga/Wangen, Gargazzone
text: A gravestone at the old parish church of Gargazzone: “Qui riposa Luigi Gruber ex Sindaco di Vanga nato 1865 morto 8.2.1935. R.I.P.” Alois Gruber, mayor of Wangen, lies under an Italian first name, an Italian formula and the official name of his village, number 568 in the decree of 1923.
That German inscriptions on graves were forbidden is often said. No decree saying so was found.
facts: Commons title 'Grabstein Alois Gruber BM Wangen in Gargazon Alte Pfarrkirche Italianisierung'; the stone names him in Italian (notes 16, §1, [V])
'Vanga' is the official name in the 1923 decree's list (no. 568) (row 16.03; notes 16, §1, [V])
No primary text for a ban on German gravestone inscriptions was found; it is asserted only in popular articles [SS] (notes 16, §1, Gaps)

entries.title: Gazzetta Ufficiale, 5 October 1935, n. 233: prefectural decrees of Bolzano on surnames
text: A dozen pages of the Gazzetta Ufficiale of 5 October 1935 filled with decrees of the prefect of Bolzano, each a “Riduzione di cognomi nella forma italiana”, each signed Mastromattei. On one page Egger becomes “Mancini”, Oberkofler “Covoli”, Castlunger “Costalunga”, Feichtinger “Fedrighi”.
Every decree says it answers a request and was posted for a month at the town hall without objection. For tracing a family, this is where the name changes.
facts: Pages 4–16 of the issue are almost wholly 'Decreti prefettizi: Riduzione di cognomi nella forma italiana', signed 'Il prefetto: Mastromattei' (notes 16, §1, [V])
Each decree cites R.D.L. 10 January 1926 n. 17 and the ministerial instructions of 5 August 1926, answers a 'domanda', and was posted for a month at the commune without objections (notes 16, §1, [V])

entries.title: Der Sciliar, July–August 1938, masthead
text: The masthead of South Tyrol's monthly for local history in the summer of 1938. The magazine is “Der Schlern”, after the mountain; here it appears as “Der Sciliar”, the Italian name forced into a German title and still set in Fraktur, over a vignette of the massif itself.
When the forced title began and when it ended has not been established.

entries.title: Atesia Augusta. Rassegna mensile dell'Alto Adige, anno I, 1939
text: The regime's own monthly for the province, first issue, March 1939. The prefect chairs its committee; the publisher is the provincial fascist press cooperative. It opens with a portrait of Mussolini and his handwritten dedication to the review “che ha nel nome il programma”. The title is set in Roman capitals, “ATESIA AVGVSTA”, and the price is “LIRE QVATTRO”.

Inside: Tolomei, “Terra d'Italia”, Giovanni Brusin, “Romanità dell'Alto Adige”, and aerial photographs of the new workers' blocks. The back cover is the Monument to Victory. Issue 9 carried an unsigned article on the Option accords.
facts: No. 1, March 1939: 'Presidente del Comitato Direttivo dott. Giuseppe Mastromattei', 'Redattore-Capo Responsabile Giuseppe Silvestri', 'Editore: Ente Cooperativo Provinciale della Stampa Fascista', 'Tipografia Ferrari Auer S.A. Bolzano', 'Copertina di Guido Pelizzari' (notes 16, §2, [V])

Opens with a portrait credited 'Ghitta Carell' and a handwritten dedication read as 'Alla Rivista Atesia Augusta che ha nel nome il programma con fervido augurio fascista – Roma 25 febb. XVII – Mussolini' (notes 16, §2, [V, reading of the hand])

Contents include Ettore Tolomei 'Terra d'Italia', Giovanni Brusin 'Romanità dell'Alto Adige', Carlo Battisti 'Il Dizionario Toponomastico Atesino', Giuseppe Silvestri 'Clima di rinascita' with aerials 'Fot. Pedrotti' (notes 16, §§1–2, [V]; the authors read on the contents page, 17 Nov. 2026)

The 1939 index (in no. 10) lists 'Bolzano ai Caduti per l'Impero' (no. 4), Mastromattei 'Serenità operosa' (no. 8) and an unsigned 'L'esecuzione degli accordi italo-germanici per i Tedeschi dell'Alto Adige' (no. 9) (notes 16, §2, [V])
Title set in Roman capitals with V for U ('AVGVSTA', 'LIRE QVATTRO'); the back cover prints the Victory Monument (notes 16, §2, [V])
BPI holds only nos. 1 and 10 of 1939; the 1941 director's name is 'Antonio Baldini Rualis', which corrects the AZ OCR in notes 03 §4 (notes 16, §2, [V])

Seen in the image (cover): brown paper, 'ATESIA AVGVSTA – RASSEGNA MENSILE DELL'ALTO ADIGE' in dark Roman capitals, a small brown drawing of a round crenellated tower and a fir tree before mountains, 'ANNO I° N 1 BOLZANO-MARZO 1939 XVII'; a library label and the 'BPI' watermark.
Seen in the image (back cover): the Victory Monument's colonnade and steps printed small in brown in the centre of a plain brown cover, 'LIRE QVATTRO' at lower right.

Seen in the image (p. 11): headline 'CLIMA DI RINASCITA' and an aerial photograph of rows of new apartment blocks captioned 'Un poderoso gruppo di novissime abitazioni operaie nel rione Littorio di Bolzano (Fot. Pedrotti)'.
Seen in the image (index pp. 58–59): 'Indice generale dell'anno 1939 XVII/XVIII', issue by issue from 'N. 1 — Marzo' to 'N. 10 — Dicembre'.

entries.title: Landsleute! Anonymous leaflet against emigration in the Option
text: A leaflet against leaving, from the autumn of the Option, headed “Landsleute!”. The German government, it says, means to move the South Tyroleans “nach Galizien”: “Für Galizien? Kennt Ihr das Land?” It names the rumour of resettlement in the south, “das sizilianische Gespenst”, and urges: “unterschreibe niemals eine Auswanderungserklärung”.
It is anonymous and typewritten, not printed. The sheet is torn off at the foot, mid-sentence.
facts: Typewritten leaflet: the German government proposes to move the South Tyroleans 'nach Galizien'; 'Für Galizien? Kennt Ihr das Land?'; 'unterschreibe niemals eine Auswanderungserklärung'; it names 'das sizilianische Gespenst' (notes 16, §6, [V])
'bis spätestens 31.Dezember diese Jahres' (as typed) dates it to autumn 1939 [INF] (notes 16, §6)
'Kennt Ihr das Land?' turns Goethe's line, used on Lenhart's UTA poster for Merano, against the Nazi promise (notes 16, §6, [INF]; notes 01, Q4)
Commons: PD-old; the file page says its copyright status 'is currently discussed' (manifest)
Seen in the image: a creased, torn and stained sheet, typed in one block with underlinings, headed 'Landsleute!'; the bottom edge is torn away mid-sentence.

entries.title: Heim ins Reich! Hand-drawn Option poster
text: A hand-painted poster for leaving: a couple in costume, seen from behind, hold a child up to a sun that rises over the mountains with a swastika in it. “Heim ins Reich!” is lettered by hand in Fraktur.
Date, maker and owner rest on the person who uploaded it to Wikimedia Commons, where a request to delete it for doubtful rights has been open since May 2026. It is a lead, not yet a document.

entries.title: Scheda individuale – Schedario degli allogeni tedeschi che hanno optato per la Germania
text: The Italian state's index card for a person who chose Germany, headed “SCHEDARIO DEGLI ALLOGENI TEDESCHI CHE HANNO OPTATO PER LA GERMANIA”. On the back: “ha optato a Parcines”, and stamps of 8 April 1948, when the same card served for the re-option.

The word is “allogeni”, of another stock: the administrative name for the province's Germans, kin to the “scuole alloglotte” of the 1923 school decree. Wikimedia Commons files the card, wrongly, as a German voting card.
facts: An Italian index card for optants; back: 'Ha optato per la cittadinanza germanica con dichiarazione sul modello giallo … ha optato a Parcines', stamps 'Modello I presentato il 8 APR 1948' and 'Ricevuta prefettizia riopzione N. 13548/1' (notes 16, §6, [V])
Commons calls it 'Stimmkarte für die Option für das deutsche Reich'; the card is a prefectural index card reused for the 1948 re-option (notes 16, §6, [V card; INF link])
The word 'allogeni' links it to the 'scuole alloglotte' of the 1923 school decree (row 16.05) (notes 16, §6, [INF])
Personal data blacked out by the uploader; CC0 (manifest)

Seen in the image (front): an orange card headed 'SCHEDA INDIVIDUALE' with an alphabet strip A–Z and 'SCHEDARIO DEGLI ALLOGENI TEDESCHI CHE HANNO OPTATO PER LA GERMANIA'; black bars over the names; 'Lagundo', 'Bolzano', 'Merano' typed in; a faint diagonal stamp about revocation.
Seen in the image (back): printed questions on emigration, passport and German citizenship; typed 'ha optato a Parcines'; violet stamps dated 8 April 1948 and a receipt number 13548/1.

entries.title: Albert Stolz, Heimat und Front 1941–1942
text: A postcard of 1941–42 signed by Albert Stolz and issued, according to Wikimedia Commons, by the optants' association for the winter relief. A triptych: a woman and two children lifting potatoes, soldiers in steel helmets with a grenade, and between them an eagle over a wreathed swastika with “Heimat und Front 1941-1942” in Fraktur.
Field and grenade, home and front: the optants' own organisation carrying the Reich's war imagery in South Tyrol.

entries.title: Enzo Ianes, 'L'asilo è il mezzo più potente per la penetrazione dell'italianità'. Il ruolo dell'Opera Nazionale Assistenza Italia Redenta nel processo di italianizzazione dell'Alto Adige
text: A study of the kindergartens that the Opera Nazionale di Assistenza all'Italia Redenta ran in the German-speaking valleys: about fifty by December 1927, about a hundred at the end of the 1930s. Its title is a quotation: “L'asilo è il mezzo più potente per la penetrazione dell'italianità”. In Bolzano's Rencio quarter the clandestine German kindergartens were closed by the authorities in 1937.
It names the archive files that hold the story of each kindergarten.
facts: Geschichte und Region/Storia e regione 28 (2019), 2, pp. 111–142 (manifest)
ONAIR, founded 1919; 'nel dicembre 1927 … circa 50 asili nelle zone tedesche dell'Alto Adige', about a hundred at the end of the 1930s (notes 16, §3, [S])
From 1924/25 Rosa and Carolina Agazzi ran the 'Asilo Principessa Mafalda di Bolzano' as the training kindergarten (notes 16, §3, [S])
'nel quartiere Rencio di Bolzano nel 1937 furono chiusi dalle autorità gli asili clandestini in lingua tedesca' (notes 16, §3, [S])
Archive pointers: APTn and SLA, Fondo ONAIRC; APTn ONAIRC b. 145 'provincia di Bolzano: storia di singoli asili infantili' (notes 16, §3, Leads)

entries.title: House-number plate '26 SOPRABOLZANO'
entries.date: plate undated (fascist era per the uploader); photographed 2024
text: A house-number plate still on a wall in Soprabolzano, photographed in 2024: white enamel, blue rim, “26” and the village name in Italian only. The uploader calls it a relic “aus der Zeit der gewaltsamen Italianisierung”.
The plate's age rests on that statement alone. It is kept as a lead: the place-name decree at the scale of a single door.
